assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology led to incretin therapies that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with proven cardiovascular and renal benefit. Originality, clarity of mechanism and breadth of impact on patients are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Holst (incretin physiology and GLP-1 secretion/action) and Drucker (GLP-1 biology, GLP-2 and translational work) are central; Knudsen represents the drug-development step (liraglutide, semaglutide). Mojsov's contribution to peptide identification is credited in the list and her priority relative to others is contested; I cannot resolve that from the supplied text. Other foundational contributors outside the credited names may exist.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple large randomized outcome trials and widespread clinical use for more than a decade; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit between basic discovery and industrial drug development, and Mojsov's role, are unresolved
Whether a laureate from industry is appropriate for this prize configuration
My recollection of the detailed priority history is not independently verified

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies, a new therapeutic modality with approved products and a broad ongoing field.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (second-generation costimulatory CARs, preclinical rationale), June (clinical translation and first durable responses in CLL/ALL) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early gene-engineered T cell trials) form a plausible trio. Eshhar and others outside the credited names are not available on this list.
assessment.maturity: Mature for hematologic cancers with long-term follow-up and regulatory approvals; solid tumours, toxicity and access remain unresolved but do not undermine the core discovery.
uncertainties: Credit for the original chimeric receptor concept falls partly outside the credited names
Long-term safety, including secondary malignancy, is still being evaluated
Choice among Rosenberg, June and Sadelain is debatable

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical precancer, with population data showing sharp declines in cervical disease. A clear, original, high-impact preventive medicine achievement.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed the L1 VLP approach; Frazer (with Zhou) contributed independent VLP production and the clinical path. This triple is coherent, though other groups (including Zhou's, who died in 1999) and company work complicate priority.
assessment.maturity: Mature: long-term efficacy and effectiveness data, including reductions in invasive cervical cancer in vaccinated cohorts, are now available. Timely.
uncertainties: Parallel independent inventions and the late Jian Zhou's contribution complicate attribution
Prize committee precedent for the HPV virus discovery (2008) may affect the view of the vaccine step

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology a causal tool for controlling genetically defined cells with light, enabling circuit-level discoveries across the brain and beyond, with early therapeutic applications for vision restoration.
assessment.attribution: The channelrhodopsin discovery and characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) and its deployment in neurons (Boyden, Deisseroth) are both decisive; Miesenböck's earlier light-gated approach adds a further claimant. With six credited names, any three-person selection leaves out a legitimate contributor.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a research tool, with a very large body of independent use; clinical translation is early but not needed for a tool-based prize.
uncertainties: Six credible contributors against a three-person limit makes a fair allocation difficult
Possible contention about whether the prize should honour discovery of the channel or its neuronal application
Relative contributions of Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck not independently verified

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined an intracellular signalling pathway from the ER to the nucleus, with consequences for protein quality control, diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. Conceptually original and clear.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori established the pathway in yeast and mammals (Ire1, Hac1/Xbp1 splicing), a natural pair. Others in the field (for example in mammalian PERK/ATF6 branches) are not in the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed over decades; disease relevance is documented, though direct therapeutic validation is still developing.
uncertainties: Therapeutic impact is less established than for the top-ranked candidates
Credit for the mammalian branches may be incomplete

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted inhibition of BCR-ABL turned chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease into a manageable chronic condition and established the paradigm of molecularly targeted cancer therapy.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical development and rationale), Lydon (compound discovery at Ciba-Geigy/Novartis) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) are a plausible trio. Upstream recognition of the BCR-ABL fusion (Rowley, Groffen, Baltimore and others) is outside the credited names, which may raise a fairness question.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than two decades of survival data and a validated drug class; recognition is somewhat delayed but not premature.
uncertainties: Whether foundational fusion-gene discoveries should share recognition
Industry versus academic credit weighting

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-frequency deep brain stimulation changed the treatment of advanced Parkinson's disease and movement disorders and has become a widely used neuromodulation approach. As a neurologist I judge the clinical effect robust and durable, while acknowledging the bias risk from my field.
assessment.attribution: Benabid's initial demonstration of thalamic and then subthalamic high-frequency stimulation is decisive. Contributions from DeLong (basal ganglia circuitry, subthalamic target rationale) and others are not available in the credited list, so a single-laureate configuration may be incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of randomized trials, long-term follow-up and broad adoption. Timely or overdue.
uncertainties: Credit shared with basal ganglia physiologists and neurosurgeons not on the list
Whether a device and surgical technique fit the prize's discovery criterion as strongly as a biological mechanism
Possible perceived bias from the chair's neurological field

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of PCSK9 as a gene altering LDL cholesterol, and its human genetics, led rapidly to antibody and siRNA therapies that lower LDL and cardiovascular risk. A strong example of genetics-to-drug translation.
assessment.attribution: Abifadel and colleagues (with Boileau) identified gain-of-function mutations in familial hypercholesterolemia, Seidah characterized the proprotein convertase biology, and Hobbs and Cohen showed that loss-of-function variants lower LDL and protect against coronary disease. Five credited names against a three-laureate limit makes allocation hard.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature: approved drugs with outcome-trial benefit, though the field is younger than the higher-ranked candidates and long-term data continue to accrue.
uncertainties: Five contributors and no clear three-person subset
Relative weight of the Paris and Dallas discoveries versus protein biochemistry
Recognition may be somewhat early compared with older candidates
